pf.license.need: A switch from the state's form. Cooking only in the customer's own kitchen usually needs no food permit, so the business gives its registration, or a business license where the state or city asks for one.

pf.rules.records: Contracts, receipts and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work. Allergy notes deleted the day after the dinner.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for a private chef:
private chef: The guest count changes before the final count: a new total to OK; over the chef's limit needs the owner's OK
The final count isn't in by its day: the contract's count is billed, and the owner calls about allergies
A severe allergy note: the booking waits for the chef's OK, and the allergy plate is made apart
The oven or a burner doesn't work: the chef cooks another way, never changing the menu or the price
Groceries cost more than the estimate: the customer's yes first, or the chef swaps an item at the same price
The lead chef can't come on a date that can't move: a chef with the skill or one the owner trusts, only with the customer's yes; a new date; or a full refund
The server can't come: the owner books another; the customer isn't asked when nothing changes
The customer moves the date: a new date if a chef is free
The customer cancels: only what the contract says is kept, plus groceries already bought, with the owner's OK
A guest under 21 at a dinner with wine: no wine for them
A dish made ahead away from the home: only in a permitted kitchen; a lapsed permit means a menu cooked in the customer's kitchen
The party runs late: extra time only with the customer's written yes; service given has no cancel period
